title: 2023 regional budget: transit, homelessness funding and police
subtitle: Transit fares, symphony and grants, bunker removal, rural mobility reserve, and defeated tax cut and airport fee proposals
overview: On budget day the committee worked through the 2023 regional budget, which sets the property tax levy and spending for regional services and police. It recommended the main budget motion for regional services {{vote:m43}}, along with the Waterloo Regional Police Service budget at a slightly higher net expenditure than the Police Services Board proposal {{vote:m42}}.

On transit, the committee recommended the 2023 Grand River Transit service expansion {{vote:m2}}, kept the affordable transit program {{vote:m9}} and recommended a 2.5% general fare increase from July 1 {{vote:m10}}. Other fare changes, including a larger discount for low-income riders and an extended family day pass, were deferred to the transit business plan {{vote:m11}}. Proposals to add homelessness funding for community agencies were defeated {{vote:m3}} {{vote:m4}}, as were one-time requests from two community organizations {{vote:m22}} {{vote:m23}}.

The committee also recommended removing the Regional Bunker project from the 10-year capital forecast {{vote:m19}} and using $400,000 from the Rural Mobility Plus reserve to lower the 2023 levy {{vote:m20}}. Proposals for further levy cuts, higher transit passes and higher airport fees were defeated. These are recommendations that Council will consider later.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended the 2023 Plan, operating budget and capital budget for regional services excluding police, as amended during the day, with a property tax levy of $468,826,678.

The committee recommended the Waterloo Regional Police Service 2023 operating budget with a net expenditure of $236,742,817 and a property tax levy of $214,060,266, plus the capital budget and forecast.
The committee recommended adding 41,400 net annual service hours, the Cambridge network redesign by fall 2023, extending the Route 79 Breslau pilot and removing routes 2 and 73.
After reconsidering the earlier deferral, the committee recommended a 2.5% general fare increase effective July 1, 2023.
The committee deferred a larger affordable transit discount, an extended family day pass and a review of senior and youth fares to the new transit business plan.
The committee recommended taking no action on the Kitchener-Waterloo Symphony's one-time funding request, which can still apply through the normal grant process.
The committee recommended removing the Regional Bunker project from the 10-year capital budget and forecast.
The committee recommended using $400,000 from the Rural Mobility Plus reserve to reduce the 2023 property tax levy by the same amount.

debate: On the $1.2 million homelessness request, opponents said the Region would be setting policy on the fly and that a funding plan should come first through the housing and homelessness master plan. Supporters said needs were urgent, funds set aside would only be spent with Council approval, and staff could allocate it equitably.

On a half-sized $600,000 amendment, one councillor argued money should be set aside now because requests would arrive during the year anyway. Others worried that a fund would invite requests from every agency and noted that some organizations may not have known they could ask.

On later one-time requests for two community organizations, councillors said they valued the work but disagreed on whether to fund them without a grant process. Staff said housing and homelessness has no discretionary grant policy, and the CAO suggested the strategic planning process as the place to decide this.

On transit fares, some councillors wanted pilots such as free fares for children and seniors and others wanted them left to the master planning process. A deferral of the whole item was passed, then reconsidered so the 2.5% increase, which supporters tied to rising operating costs, could be voted on separately.

On proposals to cut the levy, staff said a $8 million reduction was not practical from the suggested fee changes. Staff warned a university pass increase could breach agreements, that higher airport fees could risk airline service, and that cuts would likely mean service reductions.
